module_title: Introduction to UNESCO and the First Indian Sites
introduction: UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization) identifies and protects places or traditions around the world that are of outstanding value to humanity. As of recent updates (2023-2024), India has exactly **42 World Heritage Sites** (34 Cultural, 7 Natural, and 1 Mixed).

core_concepts.title: The First Sites of India (1983)
core_concepts.description:
India's journey with UNESCO began in 1983 when four iconic monuments were added simultaneously: 
1. **Taj Mahal** (Agra, UP)
2. **Agra Fort** (Agra, UP)
3. **Ajanta Caves** (Maharashtra)
4. **Ellora Caves** (Maharashtra)

core_concepts.title: Iconic Cultural Sites
core_concepts.description:
1. **Sun Temple, Konark** (Odisha) - Added in 1984. 
2. **Khajuraho Group of Monuments** (Madhya Pradesh) - Added in 1986. 
3. **Hampi Monuments** (Karnataka) - Added in 1986. 
4. **Sanchi Stupa** (Madhya Pradesh) - Added in 1989.

core_concepts.title: Mountain Railways of India
core_concepts.description:
UNESCO recognizes three spectacular mountain railways in India collectively: 
1. Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (West Bengal)
2. Nilgiri Mountain Railway (Tamil Nadu)
3. Kalka-Shimla Railway (Himachal Pradesh)

important_entities.name: UNESCO Headquarters
important_entities.significance: A fundamental Static GK question. The headquarters of UNESCO is located in Paris, France.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Students usually memorize monuments, but UNESCO also recognizes entire cities. **Ahmedabad** (2017) was the first Indian city to get UNESCO World Heritage status, followed by **Jaipur** (2019).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
A - Ajanta Caves 
A - Agra Fort

exam_strategy_tips: A guaranteed SSC CHSL/CGL question: 'Which was the first city in India to be inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list?' Answer: Ahmedabad.
